We started seeing a big jump in P95/P99 latency and a ~4-6% error rate across our inference routes after the model variant flip you ran last night (you can see the Grafana snapshot attached). Traffic patterns and input distribution didn't change on our side. Specifics:

- P95: from ~120ms -> ~420ms
- P99: from ~220ms -> ~1.2s
- Error rate: from 0.2% -> 4.9% (mostly 5xx decode errors)
- Throughput: overall token throughput is down ~18% despite steady request rate

This is affecting user flows and our payments pipeline — leadership is on this. Can you confirm whether the new quantization profile v3.1 is in use for our production routing? If so, we need immediate rollback or an emergency workaround. Attaching a couple of screenshots and an error sample.

Please escalate — our CTO is expecting updates.

From: markus.klein@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Production spike after quant v3.1 deploy — urgent

Quick triage notes (initial):
- We see a statistically significant increase in decode time for the v3.1 quant path on the T4 fleet handling BridgeView traffic. Root cause hypothesis: new kernel selection for v3.1 triggers an attention kernel that spills to host memory at higher sequence lengths (~512+), causing CPU stall and increased p99.
- Error sample indicates repeated 5xx from decoder OOM fallback — not full GPU OOM but device-to-host fallback path.

Short-term mitigations I can apply now (need ops approval):
1) Pin BridgeView routing to the previous model variant (v3.0-baseline) — instantaneous.
2) Reduce per-request max_seq to 384 for BridgeView traffic via routing override — reduces spill but may truncate some long prompts.
3) Roll forward a hotfix kernel that avoids the problematic codepath (takes ~3 hours to validate).

Given customer impact and exec attention, I recommend option 1 immediately. I can push routing pin within 20 minutes. If ops prefer, option 2 can be a short-term stopgap while I stage the hotfix.

-Markus
Markus Klein
